svg.aria-label: From book project to edition — a managed textbook build
svg.title: From book project to edition — a managed textbook build

g.text: From book project to edition — a managed textbook build
Reviews are patch proposals with sign-offs. One pipeline validates, scans, renders site/PDF/EPUB, builds the pack and signs it with a key that never leaves KMS.
1 · Editors and reviewers approve changes as patch proposals; each sign-off is bound to the exact proposal hash.
2 · The author freezes the edition locally and asks for a managed build of site, PDF, EPUB and pack.
3 · Only the book's allowlisted files are uploaded: private notes never leave the vault.
4 · The Books API handles the request.
5 · It checks the review rules: no self-approval; dosing and monograph changes need two clinical reviewers.
6 · The book pipeline starts for this edition and revision.
7 · Validate: every cross-reference, citation and figure resolves, alt text exists, no private document is referenced.
8 · Medical profile: text and image metadata are scanned for patient data; findings block the build.
9 · Render the hosted site, PDF and EPUB from the same AST (parallel builds).
10 · Build the Knowledge Pack: content, files.json, partitions, FTS and graph indexes.
11 · Embeddings for large books use Bedrock batch inference; namespace = model + version.
12 · Site, PDF and EPUB are written to a new edition prefix.
13 · Macie scans the outputs; a high-severity finding blocks release.
14 · Pack files are stored by content hash, so errata and new editions upload only what changed.
15 · The pack manifest is signed with the publisher's KMS key (ECDSA P-256); the private key never leaves KMS.
16 · After the publisher approves the release, the edition or erratum revision is listed in the catalog.
